note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent auditor) after 53c17be5e3. RFC 5216 Section 2.1.1: 'If the peer's sessionId is null or unrecognized by the server, the server MUST choose the sessionId to establish a new session.' Producer: the patched GOROOT doFullHandshake (internal/le/go/stdpatch/patches/crypto-tls-server-session-id.patch) writes a fresh 32-octet session_id when the TLS 1.2 full handshake issues no ticket, and eap_tls.go::tls12WithoutTickets disables tickets for every handshake negotiatesTLS13 classifies as TLS 1.2. UNRECOGNIZED half: rfc5216_session_id_test.go::TestRFC5216TLS12FullHandshakeServerHelloSessionID offers ze's peer's non-empty random id and requires a 32-octet ServerHello session_id differing from it, no SessionTicket extension and no NewSessionTicket. NULL half: TestRFC5216TLS12NullSessionIDServerChooses rewrites the TLS 1.2 ClientHello to an empty session_id (asserted), replays it at two fresh authenticators and requires each ServerHello to carry a 32-octet id, no ticket, and the two ids to differ. Its recorded break is a panic in tls12WithoutTickets, which shows reachability only, so the auditor ran targeted mutants through go test overlays: a patched doFullHandshake that chooses an id only when the client offered one ('!ticketSupported && len(clientHello.sessionId) > 0') leaves the unrecognized-id test green and turns the null-id test red on 'session_id is 0 octets'; tls12WithoutTickets without SessionTicketsDisabled turns both red. Limit: the null-id ClientHello still carries the SessionTicket extension; the null-id ClientHello without it is not sent.
